findings.title: The 1.4× leg cap chosen in round 3 contradicts the Sprint tab's bolted thrust (1.0× the strength used) for the same horizontal push: towing a car, his body accelerates faster than his own unloaded sprint. The README doesn't say so.
findings.location: rex-strength-lab/src/engine.js:1662 (pull: `aFeet = Math.min(anc.R, LEG_SHARE() * usable) / body.m`, LEG_SHARE = MUSCLE.jump.forceFrac 1.4, whose comment says it is above 1 because 'leg extensors also carry body weight') against engine.js:1601 (sprint, bolted: `thrust = Fu`). README decision 7 justifies 1.4× only as 'the Pull tab's own leg rule'.
findings.evidence:
Engine at def9546, concrete, default dial (90,718.474 kg-force), powers on, bolted:
- P.sprint: thrust 889.6 kN, accel 296.5 m/s². 10 m from rest takes about 0.26 s, since drag is about 11 kN at the 77 m/s it reaches.
- P.pull with the car, all-out: his legs push his own body with walkPush.J/T = 1,245.5 kN, accel 415.2 m/s², t10m 0.2195 s. That is while also pulling the 1,340 kg car with 556 kN.

So the same legs, on the same bolted feet, pushing the same 3,000 kg body forward, get 1.4× the strength on Pull and 1.0× on Sprint. Dragging a car, Rex covers 10 m (0.22 s) and reaches 100 km/h (0.067 s) faster than he can sprint unloaded (0.26 s and 0.094 s).

The 1.4 factor is the leg-extension rule, and its extra 0.4 is the body weight the legs carry vertically. The pull applies it to a horizontal push. Round 3's reviewer offered both caps ('or, matching Sprint's bolted thrust, Math.min(anc.R, usable)'). The choice is recorded, but not this consequence.
findings.expected: Either the two tabs use one rule for his legs' horizontal push on bolted feet, or the README (decision 7) and the Pull tab say why the Pull's legs out-push the Sprint's, and that a towed load therefore goes faster than his own sprint.
findings.fix:
Preferred: use Sprint's rule in pull(), `aFeet = Math.min(anc.R, usable) / body.m` (bolted all-out car 0.26 s; light loads under about 3,000 kg go at his body's pace). Then update 5d's 1.4 checks, the page's 'at most 1.4×' phrases, the README decision 7 and What moved figures, and the PR draft.

Otherwise keep 1.4× and add a sentence to README decision 7 (and the Pull item) saying Sprint's bolted thrust is 1.0× the strength used, so a pull's steps can out-accelerate his sprint.

verdict.reasoning:
Reproduced on the engine and on the rendered page. Bolted, at the default dial, all powers on:
- Sprint: 'Push-off = the strength he uses (bolted: no friction or soft-ground limit)', 890 kN, so 296.5 m/s².
- Pull: 'His legs still move his own body, with at most 1.4× the strength he uses (1.25 MN)', so 415.2 m/s².

It is the same 3,000 kg body, the same legs and the same bolted feet pushing level. Sprint's friction thrust, min(Fu, μN), is exactly pull's aFeet, min(anc.R, LEG·usable), with LEG = 1, so the two tabs use one formula with two different leg factors.

Result: dragging a car (or any load under about 2,100 kg), he covers 10 m in 0.22 s and ends at 91 m/s (the page states his body's momentum, 270,000 kg·m/s). His unloaded sprint takes 0.267 s over 10 m with its own drag and leg-speed cap, tops out at 61.1 m/s ('His legs set the top speed') and reaches 100 km/h in 0.094 s, against the pull's 0.067 s. Adding a load makes him faster, which a reader will catch.

The 1.4 factor's own comment ties it to vertical leg extension ('leg extensors also carry body weight, which a deadlift record excludes'). README decision 7 justifies it only as 'the Pull tab's own leg rule'. Neither it nor Known limits mentions Sprint's 1.0× or this consequence, and decision 13 says the sprint is unchanged.

The 1.4× choice is recorded and arguable: bolted, the legs' total extension force could go mostly horizontal. So this is not wrong physics outright. It is an unstated cross-tab contradiction created by round 3 (main's bolted pull went at the pair's pace, 0.31 s, slower than the sprint). Minor.

One caveat on the finding's preferred fix. Even at 1.0×, the pull would reach 77 m/s at 10 m in 0.26 s, still past Sprint's 61.1 m/s leg-speed top speed, because the pull applies no leg-speed cap. That smaller gap already existed on main: the pair pace reached 64 m/s. So the fix should also state the missing leg-speed cap.

Minimal, keeping round 3's 1.4×: add a sentence to README decision 7 (and Known limits), and a clause to the Pull tab's bolted item:
